name: OpenAPI route map → object IDOR sweep
trigger_hint: API schema discovered — convert it into a route map, then IDOR lanes per object type

preconditions.how: GET /openapi.json with EACH captured credential (401-gated schemas often open with the bypass/admin token)

steps.note: with every credential; the schema itself is an attack surface
parse paths × methods; group by object (anything with an id-like field); list auth requirements per route
the IDOR worklist: endpoint shapes reached by 2+ credentials
per object: replay A's IDs with B's session — differential gates the verdict
schema-typed params: integer/string/format fields get class-appropriate probes

exit: schema parsed OR 2 fetch attempts fail on every credential

name: XSS primitive → session/token theft
trigger_hint: Script execution context reachable — turn it into token theft

preconditions.how: inject_probe vuln_class=xss — tag survival + sink context first

steps.note: survival battery before crafting — know the sink (HTML/attr/JS)
POC: read document.cookie + localStorage token keys, shape = alert(JSON.stringify(...)) — never exfil off-scope
confirm with the marker-from-stdout gate, not a screenshot of an alert

exit: token readable in POC OR sink escapes every payload class

name: JWT attack surface
trigger_hint: JWT in play — check the classic confusion family

preconditions.how: any response/auth header carrying a JWT (creds are auto-stored)

steps.note: decode header+claims: alg, exp, role claims, kid presence
alg:none replay; alg-confusion (HS256 with the public key) when jwk/jku/x5c in header; kid injection paths
expired-token acceptance + role-claim escalation, one variable at a time

exit: signature bypass OR claim escalation confirmed OR all confusion classes gated

name: Object-level IDOR sweep
trigger_hint: Object IDs in responses — cross-user access is the classic win

preconditions.how: request_auth — two sessions make IDOR testable

steps.note: the worklist is already built from your request history
A's object IDs under B's session; the 3-gate diff decides
record with the differential evidence attached

exit: worklist drained OR every lane gated

name: 403 → what's actually behind the door
trigger_hint: A 403 is a locked door, not a wall — enumerate what opens it

steps.note: ~24 variants; the tool must list what was NOT tried if it fails
high-value routes BEHIND the gate: /v1/admin /v1/users /v1/tokens /internal — one quiet sweep
any bypass token found replays against the schema/rotes it unlocks

exit: bypass confirmed OR every variant + route sweep exhausted

name: SSRF → internal network map
trigger_hint: Server-side fetch of a URL you control — map the internal network

preconditions.how: a URL parameter the SERVER fetches (response diff or timing proves it)

steps.note: collaborator-style canary first (if out of scope: internal-only targets — 127.0.0.1, metadata IPs) — NEVER cloud metadata outside authorized scope
internal sweep: 127.0.0.1:PORT/ high-value ports; differential gates each claim
confirmed internal reach = a finding even without data return (response/time oracle counts)

exit: internal service reached OR primitive disproven

name: Upload → code execution
trigger_hint: File upload surface — the path to webshell/RCE

steps.note: extension/content-type/magic-byte matrix — one variable per request; note which validation layer bites
locate the stored file (path traversal in the filename writes outside uploads/)
the POC prints a marker AFTER server-side execution — echo-marker alone proves nothing

exit: server-side execution OR every bypass class gated

name: Exposed .git → source + secrets
trigger_hint: Repository metadata readable — reconstruct the source

steps.note: reconstruct: fetch objects via the HTTP dumb protocol, or git-dumper if installed
sweep the tree for secrets: history (git log -p), configs, keys — creds_add every live one
source now guides EVERY other lane — read the auth code before the next auth attack

name: GraphQL map → field abuse
trigger_hint: GraphQL endpoint — introspection writes your attack map

steps.note: full introspection query; if disabled: clue-hunting via error messages and suggested fields
field-level authz: query each object type as user B — field IDORs are the GraphQL classic
mutations take user input like anything else

exit: schema mapped OR introspection fully gated

name: RCE/foothold → internal network access
trigger_hint: Command execution confirmed — pivot to the internal network

steps.note: recon INSIDE: hostname, ip, arp, /etc/hosts, listening services — read-only first
internal hosts, then top ports on the interesting ones
each internal service = evidence; lateral paths come from the map

exit: internal map drawn OR egress fully blocked

name: Linux privilege escalation
trigger_hint: Linux foothold — enumerate the escalation surface

preconditions.how: shell on a Linux host (from rce_to_internal)

steps.note: the enumeration triad: sudo -l, SUID find, cron + writable paths — one command, read it all
kernel version + search_cve for local privesc; sudo version for the classic CVEs
POC marks root with `id` output AFTER the exploit runs

exit: root OR surface fully enumerated and gated

name: Container escape
trigger_hint: You're inside a container — the escape surface is specific

steps.note: mounts (privileged?), capabilities (capsh --print), socket exposure, hostPID
runc/CVE family by version; socket mount = the direct path
escape POC must prove HOST context (hostname change or /host file read)

exit: host context reached OR container hardened

name: Stolen token → account takeover proof
trigger_hint: A usable session token — prove the takeover end-to-end

steps.note: store the token the moment you hold it (server-side; reference the env var, never the literal)
read the victim's own profile/identity endpoint — access to someone ELSE'S data is the proof
record with the identity-response evidence

exit: foreign identity accessed OR token rejected

name: Schema-typed fuzz lanes
trigger_hint: Typed API params — fuzz with the RIGHT payload classes

steps.note: integer fields → overflow/negative/string-where-int; string+format → injection classes by sink; boolean → type juggling
class-appropriate batteries only — no payload soup
baseline vs probe — noise floors first

exit: every typed field class-tested OR gates on all
